pr_body:
Solves: #16968 

**Description**:
Added force re-render mechanism for components.

**Support**:
As @bvaughn suggested, we will **only support React 16.9+**
Versions that aren't supported won't show the `re-render` button in the UI.

**Tested on**:
- Versions that are < 16.9 do not show the `re-render` button in the UI.
- Versions that are >= 16.9 show the `re-render` button in the UI and successfully dispatch an update to the supported components types.

![re-render](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23095052/66699917-6657a380-eceb-11e9-9cbe-4228b1655479.gif)
pr_comments:
No significant bundle size changes to report.

I think we could improve the UX a bit though. When you click the button, there's no confirmation or signal that it's actually been clicked. Nothing happens.

Maybe we need to make it stay highlighted for a second :think: or something. Thoughts?
I guess I still don't quite understand the use case of this feature, so I'd like to hold off merging it for the time being until I understand it better, and we work out the UX issue.
Heya @bvaughn ! I'll address your comments and after that we can park it for the time being, until we get more feature requests like this one? What do you think?

Sounds good, and thanks for being so understanding.

The code approach here seems fine. I'm just not sure the feature itself makes total sense yet, until I better understand the use case :)

We chatted on #16968 and agreed to close this for now.

Thanks a bunch for the PR though!

Hey @bvaughn! Hope you are doing well.

I'm struggling to find a good way to re-render the component that will capture all use cases. 

I used `instance.forceUpdate` but this doesn't capture all use cases - for example functional components. 

I can push my code if you want to check it out and advise if possible?
You should push it if you'd like someone to look it over. I don't know if I'll have any time in the near future though. Going to be pretty busy preparing for React conf.

I will say that I don't think `instance.forceUpdate` is the right way to go though.

You might try using the `scheduleUpdate` function injected into the renderer, although this would only work for v16.9+ (but I think that's okay).

Looked at @hristo-kanchev's PR this morning and the code looks good, but I realized something was bugging me about the feature request. I don't understand the use case here.

If your component is pure, forcing a re-render should be a no-op. (The output should be the same since the inputs didn't change.) So what is the purpose of doing this? Could you walk me through what you're trying to do/test/measure, @kentcdodds?

The situation is mostly to determine whether opting out of re-renders would be beneficial. In my specific case, I'm contriving examples to demonstrate the benefits of `React.memo`, but in more real-world scenarios it could be used anywhere that people think there may be a benefit to opting a tree out of unnecessary updates. It's basically a way to help them measure.

I suppose it could be argued that it'd be better for people to profile actual interactions instead though. This feature may just increase people's general unfounded fear of re-renders.

I wanted to prove to a developer they were doing something wrong by forcing a bug with a forced re-render :)

It's a shame, I wanted to step through the render method in the javascript debugger to reason about why certain things are / are not happening in my component.  It's very inconvenient to refresh the page, and go through the many steps necessary to recreate the conditions, just to have one shot at stepping through with a debugger.  One render is also wasted just to add the breakpoint, I can't even add the breakpoint ahead of time because the source code isn't immediately loaded.

@gcvs You might already be aware, but if not– check out [conditional breakpoints](https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2015/07/set-a-breakpoint-based-on-a-certain-condition). They're a great help with what you're describing.

@bvaughn Talking about breakpoints, say you place a breakpoint in code that runs on render, this feature would be perfect for triggering a rerender so that the breakpoint can be hit and you can start stepping through the code (with the use case being that you notice something wrong after the page is rendered).

@bvaughn conditional breakpoints do not help at all here with what I described.  I was not waiting for a special condition to step through a component being rendered multiple times.  Quite the opposite, I was waiting for the one and only render of a component that's lazily loaded then immediately rendered.  The component has to be loaded before I can even find it in the source tab from which to add the breakpoint.

Now, eleven months later I'm googling for a solution to the same problem, and find my own comment :). (gcvs is my account)

I'm debugging an order confirmation page. To get there, I have to navigate through checkout, which involves adding products to the basket, filling in registration details, adding payment, consents etc.  It takes a while to reach the order confirmation page.  If I use breakpoints, conditional or not, then every time I want to step through the render, I have to create a new customer and go through the checkout process again.
Essentially, it takes a long time to reproduce the exact conditions I want to test, so it's much more convenient to ask the component to re-render, than it is to create a new order from scratch.

I'm also looking for option to this. Is there any other workaround that making full page refresh? Refreshing whole page doesn't allow to debug if we are doing too much work at every render because it's expected first render will do way more. I'm interested in debugging next renders.

It is disappointing to not have a way to induce a re-render in the dev tools.

I have an awful hack for a very limited scenario.  If you want to re-render simply to hit a breakpoint in a renderer without reloading the page (and requiring a lengthy set of steps to get the app back to the current state) then I can put a `debugger` statement in my code so that hot reload will serve the change to the browser which will break on the statement.  A normal breakpoint will not work during hot reloads.
